title: Securities Trading Policy (EVN-COR-POL-003, Version 2.0)
date_approved: 1 April 2015 (amended by the Board); issued 2 April 2015

tiers.name: personnel
tiers.description: All Directors, Senior Executives, employees, contractors and consultants of Evolution and its subsidiaries. Subject to the insider trading prohibition and the absolute bans on short-term trading, short selling, margin lending/secured financing and hedging of unvested entitlements; no clearance or trading-window requirement unless in a higher tier.

tiers.name: Directors and Senior Executives
tiers.description: Directors and Senior Executives (persons who are not Directors but meet the AASB 124 definition of Key Management Personnel), together with any family member or associate over whom they have influence. May deal only in a nominated trading window with prior written clearance from the Company Secretary (Executive Chairman if the Company Secretary is dealing). Directors also have Listing Rule 3.19A/3.19B disclosure obligations.

tiers.name: designated employees
tiers.description: Employees designated by the Company Secretary at his or her discretion; subject to the same trading-window and clearance regime as Directors and Senior Executives.

tiers.name: employee insiders
tiers.description: Employees (other than Senior Executives) notified by the Company Secretary that they are on the insider list; must not deal unless clearance is given via the Securities Trading Clearance Request Form, but are not subject to the trading windows.

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company reserves the right to impose a restriction on trading during any period, including one that would otherwise fall within a permitted trading window; the Company Secretary may also designate employees as subject to trading-window restrictions at his or her discretion. Any period in which a matter constituting inside information exists is a prohibited trading period. Confidentiality of ad hoc restrictions is not addressed.

rules.detail: No express derivatives rule. 'Securities' include financial products issued or created over securities by third parties, structured financial products, swaps, futures, CFDs, spread bets, options, warrants and other derivatives, with no venue limit; 'deal' includes entering into a contract with the purpose to secure a profit or avoid a loss by reference to price fluctuations. An OTC put/call with a bank is therefore a dealing requiring written clearance from the Company Secretary, inside a trading window, with no inside information. Designated employees are treated identically; employee insiders need clearance but are not window-bound.
rules.evidence: Securities include financial products issued or created over securities by third parties, structured financial products, swaps, futures contracts, contracts for differences, spread bets, options, warrants, depository receipts or other derivatives over or related to the performance of shares.

rules.detail: For personnel outside the clearance tiers, derivatives are dealings subject only to the insider trading prohibition and the absolute bans (short-term, short selling, secured financing, hedging unvested entitlements).
rules.evidence: Entering into a contract with the purpose to secure a profit or avoid a loss by reference to price fluctuations

rules.detail: Absolute ban for all personnel on transactions with securities or any derivative thereof that limit the economic risk of unvested entitlements under an equity-based remuneration scheme, entitlements otherwise awarded, or entitlements to be offered in the future. No clearance route.
rules.evidence: enter into transactions with securities (or any derivative thereof) which limit the economic risk of any unvested entitlements awarded under an equity-based remuneration scheme, or otherwise awarded, or which will be offered by the Company in the future (eg hedging).

rules.detail: The hedging ban is confined to unvested entitlements. A hedge of vested shares is not named and is caught only as a dealing (a contract to avoid a loss by reference to price fluctuations), so it requires written clearance and a trading window. The policy does not distinguish vested-but-locked shares.
rules.evidence: Entering into a contract with the purpose to secure a profit or avoid a loss by reference to price fluctuations

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar is an agreement to dispose and so a dealing requiring clearance and a trading window; any monetisation that takes security over Evolution securities is a prohibited secured financing arrangement.
rules.evidence: Any acquisition or disposal, or agreement to acquire or dispose

rules.detail: Outright ban on short selling the Company's securities at any time, for all personnel.
rules.evidence: engage in short-term trading (less than one month), or short selling of the Company's securities at any time;

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named anywhere and is not listed in the dealing definition.

CFDs and spread bets are named only within the definition of securities, so dealing in them requires clearance and a trading window; a CFD would in practice fall within the short-term trading ban (less than one month) and, if short, the short-selling ban.
rules.evidence: Securities include ... contracts for differences, spread bets, options, warrants, depository receipts or other derivatives over or related to the performance of shares.

rules.detail: Absolute ban for all personnel on margin lending in respect of the Company's securities, at any time, with no clearance or exemption route.
rules.evidence: Personnel are not permitted at any time to: ... enter into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in respect of the Company's securities;

rules.detail: Granting security over Evolution securities to support a financing is an 'other secured financing arrangement' and prohibited. A charge or lien unconnected to a financing is not named and is not a dealing under the definition.
rules.evidence: enter into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in respect of the Company's securities;

rules.detail: Blanket ban on any secured financing arrangement in respect of the Company's securities, applying to all personnel at any time with no tier, vesting-state or approval carve-out.
rules.evidence: Personnel are not permitted at any time to: ... enter into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in respect of the Company's securities;

rules.detail: Short-term trading, defined as less than one month, is banned at any time for all personnel; no carve-outs are stated.
rules.evidence: engage in short-term trading (less than one month), or short selling of the Company's securities at any time;

clearance.approver: Company Secretary (Executive Chairman if the Company Secretary is seeking permission)
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (Directors only: information to enable Listing Rule 3.19A/3.19B and Appendix 3Y disclosure; Company Secretary notifies the Board of all Director trades)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: unspecified (Company Secretary reports to ASX and Board 'as soon as reasonably practicable')
clearance.evidence: Directors, Senior Executives and designated employees who are given clearance to deal must do so no later than five business days from clearance being received. ... The Company Secretary must give a copy of the response and clearance (if any) to the Director, Senior Executive, employee insider or designated employee requesting clearance within two business days of the initial clearance request.

Directors, Senior Executives and designated employees must complete a Securities Trading Clearance Request Form to request clearance to deal in Evolution securities and forward to the Company Secretary.

An employee insider must complete a Securities Trading Clearance Request Form to request clearance to deal in Evolution securities and forward to the Company Secretary for approval prior to executing any deal.
It is recommended that if you are unsure of the application of this Policy, you should consult the Company Secretary to clarify specific circumstances before trading is undertaken.

short_term.evidence: engage in short-term trading (less than one month), or short selling of the Company's securities at any time;

exceptions.approver: Executive Chairman (Chairperson of the Audit Committee if sought by the Executive Chairman); determination of severe financial difficulty can only be made by the Executive Chairman; request also copied to the Company Secretary
exceptions.evidence: Clearance may be given for such a person to sell (but not purchase) Evolution securities in a prohibited trading period. The determination of whether the person in question is in severe financial difficulty or whether there are other exceptional circumstances can only be made by the Executive Chairman.

exceptions.approver: Executive Chairman (Chairperson of the Audit Committee if sought by the Executive Chairman)
exceptions.evidence: A circumstance would be considered exceptional if the person in question is required by a court order to transfer or sell the Evolution securities or there is some other overriding legal requirement for him or her to do so.

Transfers of Evolution securities held in a superannuation fund or other saving scheme with an independent trustee in which a Director or Senior Executive is a beneficiary at the initial application date of the Policy (1 January 2011);
A disposal of Evolution securities arising from the acceptance of a takeover offer, scheme of arrangement or equal access buy-back;
A disposal of rights acquired under a pro rata issue; An acquisition of Evolution securities under a pro rata issue;

An acquisition of Evolution securities under a security purchase plan or a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan where; The Directors, Senior Executives or designated employee did not commence or amend their participation in the plan during a prohibited period

An investment in, or trading units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in Evolution securities) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party;

Where a Director or Senior Executive is a trustee, dealing in Evolution securities by that trust provided the Director or Senior Executive is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to deal during the closed period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently of the Director or Senior Executive;
The obtaining by a Director of a share qualification;
The acquisition of securities under an employee incentive scheme; The acquisition of securities by a trustee of an employee incentive scheme;

Trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most of Evolution's security holders, such as a security purchase plan, dividend or distribution reinvestment plan or a rights issue where the plan determines the timing and structure of the offer and this has been approved by the Board;

exceptions.approver: prior written clearance required for the plan
exceptions.evidence: Trading under a non-discretionary trading plan for which prior written clearance has been provided and where: The Director, Senior Executive or designated employee did not enter into the plan or amend the plan during a prohibited period; The trading plan does not permit the Director, Senior Executive or designated employee to exercise any influence or discretion over how, when or whether to trade; and There is no cancellation of the trading plan during a closed period other than in exceptional circumstances.

Indirect and incidental trading that occurs as a consequence of a Director, Senior Executive or designated employee dealing in securities issued by a managed investment scheme, listed investment company, exchange-traded fund or similar investment vehicle that is managed by a third party and that happens to hold Evolution securities as part of its portfolio.

exemption_authority: Company Secretary may permit dealing outside trading windows, ordinarily only in exceptional circumstances and only if the person has no price sensitive information. Under section 6, clearance in a prohibited trading period is for a sale only (not a purchase), the determination of severe financial difficulty or other exceptional circumstances can only be made by the Executive Chairman, and prior written clearance must come from the Executive Chairman (or the Chairperson of the Audit Committee if the Executive Chairman is the applicant), with the request also provided to the Company Secretary; the sale must occur within five business days. There is no authority to waive the absolute bans in section 2 (short-term trading, short selling, secured financing, hedging unvested entitlements).

bespoke_clauses.clause: Personnel are not permitted at any time to: ... enter into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in respect of the Company's securities;
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is an 'other secured financing arrangement' expressly prohibited for all personnel at any time, regardless of vesting state, with no approval or exemption route.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Deal ... Includes, in relation to securities: Any acquisition or disposal, or agreement to acquire or dispose: Entering into a contract with the purpose to secure a profit or avoid a loss by reference to price fluctuations
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A put/call collar is squarely a contract to avoid a loss by reference to price fluctuations, so entry, unwind, roll and settlement are each dealings requiring clearance and a trading window for Directors, Senior Executives and designated employees.

bespoke_clauses.clause: enter into transactions with securities (or any derivative thereof) which limit the economic risk of any unvested entitlements awarded under an equity-based remuneration scheme, or otherwise awarded, or which will be offered by the Company in the future (eg hedging).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The ban reaches entitlements 'otherwise awarded' and future offers, so the collar must be sized strictly to vested shares and a bank should confirm that no part of the hedged parcel is referable to unvested or prospective awards.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Clearance may be given for such a person to sell (but not purchase) Evolution securities in a prohibited trading period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Closed-period relief cannot cover entry into a collar or a purchase to close a written call; only an outright sale in severe financial difficulty or under a court order can be cleared, and only by the Executive Chairman.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The trading windows for Directors, Senior Executives and designated employees are: (a) For a period of thirty days after the release of the Company's half yearly results; ... (g) For a period of fifteen days following the release of the Company's quarterly reports.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy uses narrow open windows (15 or 30 days after specified releases) rather than closed periods, so the collar must be documented and executed within one of those windows and within five business days of clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company reserves the right to impose a restriction on trading during any period, including one that would otherwise fall within a permitted trading window.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A trading window can be closed without notice, which may block a scheduled unwind, roll or physical settlement of the collar.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A clearance to deal can be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances. The Company's decision to refuse clearance is final and binding on the person seeking clearance.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A cleared collar can become unexecutable between clearance and pricing, so the bank should price and sign promptly within the five-business-day validity.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Senior Executives (or any family member or associate over whom they have influence) have additional dealing restrictions
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or the secured loan through a family member, trust or controlled entity does not escape the window, clearance or secured-financing rules.

bespoke_clauses.clause: engage in short-term trading (less than one month), or short selling of the Company's securities at any time;
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar or any related share purchase/sale that is opened and closed within one month risks characterisation as short-term trading; tenor should exceed one month.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Remedial action may include a requirement that the person who sold Evolution securities in breach of the Policy to donate any profits earned to charity.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any profit from a non-compliant collar or forced sale could be required to be disgorged to charity, in addition to disciplinary action.

summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy. Section 2 prohibits all personnel, at any time, from entering into margin lending or any other secured financing arrangement in respect of the Company's securities, so a loan secured on the collared shares is banned outright with no clearance or exemption route. An unfunded collar (purchased put and written call) over vested shares is a dealing, because 'deal' includes any contract to secure a profit or avoid a loss by reference to price fluctuations and 'securities' include OTC options, swaps and other third-party derivatives; Directors, Senior Executives and designated employees may enter one only with prior written clearance from the Company Secretary, within a nominated trading window (15 or 30 days after specified releases), executed within five business days, and without price sensitive information. The collar must not limit the economic risk of any unvested entitlement, entitlement otherwise awarded or future offer, and tenor should exceed one month to avoid the short-term trading ban. Closed-period relief is available only for a sale in severe financial difficulty or under a court order, cleared by the Executive Chairman, and cannot cover collar entry or settlement.
